title: Aurat Foundation of Pakistan
description: Senior Advisor THE YOUTH COUNCIL PAKISTAN & Former Lord Mayor of Manchester, Councillor Yasmine Dar, Chairperson of the International Lobby on Kashmir, has received another prestigious recognition for her outstanding contributions to community service, women’s empowerment and advocacy for the Kashmiri people.
paragraphs: Manchester, United Kingdom 09-Oct-2026

Senior Advisor THE YOUTH COUNCIL PAKISTAN & Former Lord Mayor of Manchester, Councillor Yasmine Dar, Chairperson of the International Lobby on Kashmir, has received another prestigious recognition for her outstanding contributions to community service, women’s empowerment and advocacy for the Kashmiri people.
Councillor Yasmine Dar was honoured by the Aurat Foundation of Pakistan at a ceremony held in Manchester on Friday, 9th October, where she received an award presented by Dr Afzal Khan MP CBE.

As a Senior Advisor of THE YOUTH COUNCIL PAKISTAN and a dedicated leader of the Jammu Kashmir Self Determination Movement International (JKSDMI), Councillor Yasmine Dar has played a significant role in strengthening women’s participation and leading international lobbying efforts on Kashmir across the United Kingdom, Europe and beyond.

Her unwavering commitment to raising awareness of the suffering, human rights violations and ongoing struggle of the people of Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir has earned her widespread respect and admiration.

The entire family of THE YOUTH COUNCIL PAKISTAN & JKSDMI takes immense pride in Councillor Yasmine Dar’s achievements. Her dedication, determination and tireless efforts continue to inspire others and strengthen the international voice for the rights and self-determination of the Kashmiri people.
CouncillorYasmineDar #WomenInLeadership #YouthCouncilPK #JKSDMI

title: Delegation by Patron In Chief
originalTitle: Delegation led by Patron In Chief
description: A high-level delegation led by Patron In Chief, THE YOUTH COUNCIL PAKISTAN Raja Najabat Hussain (Sitara-e-Pakistan), Founding Chairman JKSDM International, attended a special luncheon with Pakistan’s High Commissioner to the UK, Tipu Usman, at the Pakistan High Commission in London on 8 October 2026.
paragraphs: London, United Kingdom, October 08, 2026🇵🇰🇬🇧

A high-level delegation led by Patron In Chief, THE YOUTH COUNCIL PAKISTAN Raja Najabat Hussain (Sitara-e-Pakistan), Founding Chairman JKSDM International, attended a special luncheon with Pakistan’s High Commissioner to the UK, Tipu Usman, at the Pakistan High Commission in London on 8 October 2026.
The delegation included former Lord Mayor of Manchester Councillor Yasmine Dar, Senior Advisor of the Youth Council Pakistan, along with senior JKSDMI leaders and councillors from across the UK.

The High Commissioner praised JKSDMI’s longstanding efforts to highlight the Kashmir cause, strengthen community engagement, and promote a positive image of Pakistan. Raja Najabat Hussain briefed him on JKSDMI’s lobbying in the British Parliament and political circles, and highlighted the growing role of THE YOUTH COUNCIL PAKISTAN in engaging the younger generation.

The High Commissioner presented appreciation shields to JKSDMI representatives on behalf of the Government of Pakistan. The delegation reaffirmed its commitment to a peaceful political and diplomatic campaign for the Kashmiri people’s right to self-determination.
PakistanHighCommissionLondon #UK #Diplomacy

title: 9th Asia-Pacific Climate Change Adaptation Forum (APAN)
description: United Nations Bangkok: Muhammad Shehzad Khan, President of Youth Council Pakistan, proudly represented Pakistan at the United Nations during the 9th Asia-Pacific Climate Change Adaptation Forum (APAN) — a landmark gathering jointly organized by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).
paragraphs: United Nations Bangkok: Muhammad Shehzad Khan, President of Youth Council Pakistan, proudly represented Pakistan at the United Nations during the 9th Asia-Pacific Climate Change Adaptation Forum (APAN) — a landmark gathering jointly organized by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).

Bringing together over 1,000 young leaders from 50 nations, the Forum, held under the theme “Resilience for All: Catalyzing Transformational Adaptation,” showcased the power of collaboration, shared vision, and youth-driven innovation in addressing the climate crisis across the Asia-Pacific region.

In his impactful address, Shehzad highlighted Pakistan’s commitment and challenges in the face of climate change, emphasizing the country’s minimal contribution — less than 1% of global greenhouse gas emissions — yet its immense suffering from devastating floods in Buner, Swat, Shangla, Bajaur, Swabi, and various parts of Punjab. He presented Pakistan’s case as a frontline nation of climate vulnerability and resilience.

Shehzad pledged that Youth Council Pakistan, with its vibrant and capable network of young leaders, will spearhead nationwide climate action projects in partnership with academia, government, and global institutions — promoting nature-based solutions, green innovation, and sustainable resilience models.

He reaffirmed that Pakistan’s youth stand ready to be the architects of a climate-resilient future, transforming challenges into opportunities and ensuring that no community is left behind in the fight against climate change.

The meeting concluded with a shared commitment to explore future partnerships between Pakistan, ASEAN states, and regional climate institutions to drive collective climate action

title: Diplomatic and Youth Engagement Visit to the United Kingdom
description: Islamabad / London – August 2025 — President of Youth Council Pakistan, Muhammad Shehzad Khan, concluded a highly impactful and productive visit to the United Kingdom this August, aimed at enhancing youth diplomacy, bilateral cooperation, and cultural and educational exchange between Pakistan and the UK.
paragraphs: Islamabad / London – August 2025 — President of Youth Council Pakistan, Muhammad Shehzad Khan, concluded a highly impactful and productive visit to the United Kingdom this August, aimed at enhancing youth diplomacy, bilateral cooperation, and cultural and educational exchange between Pakistan and the UK. The visit was marked by a series of high-level engagements with Members of the British Parliament, government officials, local leaders, and student representatives.

Mr. Shehzad Khan’s agenda focused on strengthening the role of parliaments in youth-led diplomacy and addressing key global issues including climate change, education, peace-building, cultural understanding, and transnational cooperation.

During his visit, Mr. Khan held important meetings with prominent Members of the UK Parliament, including: Abtisam Mohammad, MP for Sheffield and Member of the Foreign Affairs Select Committee, Richard Burgon, MP for Leeds

Barrister Yasmin Qureshi, MP for Bolton, Chairperson of the All-Party Parliamentary Group (APPG) on Pakistan, and UK Prime Minister’s Trade Envoy to Egypt, Barrister Imran Hussain, MP for Bradford, Chairperson APPG on Kashmir, Mr. Tahir Ali, MP for Birmingham, Senior Vice Chairman APPG on Kashmir Dr. Muhammad Faisal, High Commissioner of Pakistan to the UK, Raja Najabat Hussain (Sitara-e-Pakistan), Chairman JKSDMI International, Yasmin Dar, Lord Mayor of Manchester and Chairperson of the International Lobby on Kashmir
In addition, Mr. Shehzad met with local leadership including:
Councillor Asghar Khan Qureshi, Councillor Kamran Hussain, Councillor Rizwan Jalil, Councillor Neghat Basharat

Recognizing the pivotal role of students and the diaspora in international relations and soft diplomacy, Mr. Shehzad engaged with student union representatives and youth activists from leading UK universities including Bradford University, Lancaster University, Durham University, King’s College London, Teesside University, and the University of Portsmouth.

This outreach is part of a broader initiative to build a unified platform for Pakistani youth in the UK, creating opportunities for leadership, innovation, and cultural representation. “Our youth abroad are the true ambassadors of Pakistan, and engaging them is key to promoting our country’s soft image globally,” stated Mr. Shehzad.

The visit has been hailed as a milestone in youth-led international engagement and has laid the foundation for long-term partnerships in areas such as education exchange programs, cultural diplomacy, climate advocacy, and peace-building.
Youth Council Pakistan continues to lead efforts in empowering youth at the national and international levels, aligning with Pakistan’s vision of inclusive development and global cooperation.

title: Youth Diplomacy on Global Issues
description: Muhammad Shehzad Khan, President of the Youth Council Pakistan, held a high-level meeting with Abtisam Mohamed, Member of Parliament for Sheffield Central and a respected member of the Foreign Affairs Committee of the British Parliament.
paragraphs: Muhammad Shehzad Khan, President of the Youth Council Pakistan, held a high-level meeting with Abtisam Mohamed, Member of Parliament for Sheffield Central and a respected member of the Foreign Affairs Committee of the British Parliament. The dialogue took place as part of ongoing efforts to deepen youth-led cooperation between Pakistan and the United Kingdom.

The leaders discussed the critical role of youth engagement in addressing transnational challenges such as climate change, sustainable development, and global peace. Emphasizing youth as a bridge between nations, both parties explored initiatives to empower young voices across borders to drive positive action in their communities and beyond.

The conversation focused on establishing stronger cultural, educational, and environmental diplomacy between the two countries. Muhammad Shehzad Khan highlighted the need for platforms where youth from Pakistan and the UK can collaborate on innovative solutions for shared global issues. MP Abtisam Mohamed affirmed her support for youth-led diplomacy and praised the proactive approach of the Youth Council Pakistan in international dialogue.

“We must ensure young people are not only included in global discussions but are leading them,” said Muhammad Shehzad Khan. “Our meeting with MP Mohamed is a significant step towards building a generation of globally aware, culturally connected, and environmentally responsible youth leaders.”
The meeting concluded with a mutual commitment to amplify bilateral youth engagement and to work towards a sustainable and peaceful world through continued partnership and collaborative action.

title: SafeNet Cyber Awareness Drive
description: President Youth Council Pakistan Attends Launch of SafeNet Cyber Awareness Drive 2025 at NASTP
paragraphs: President Youth Council Pakistan Attends Launch of SafeNet Cyber Awareness Drive 2025 at NASTP
Islamabad – 2025

President Youth Council Pakistan, Muhammad Shehzad Khan, attended the launching ceremony of SafeNet, a pioneering initiative by IMAP, on the invitation of CEO Fatima Rashid Malik. The event marked the beginning of the Cyber Awareness Drive 2025 at the National Aerospace Science and Technology Park (NASTP), aiming to foster a culture of digital safety and resilience in Pakistan.
Speaking at the ceremony, Muhammad Shehzad Khan highlighted the strategic importance of cybersecurity in the 21st century:
“Cybersecurity is no longer a technical matter—it is a national security imperative. The future of nations will not only be defined by their military strength but also by their digital resilience.”
He elaborated on the evolving nature of security, referencing the Copenhagen School’s broader view of security that extends from traditional to non-traditional domains. He emphasized:

“From borders to cyberspace, the definition of security has transformed. Just as AI is being deployed at the US-Mexican border for surveillance and safety, Pakistan too must adopt innovative technologies to secure its digital frontiers.”
President Khan also underlined the youth’s role in shaping a secure digital Pakistan:
“Our young generation is our first line of defense against cyber threats. By equipping them with knowledge and tools, we are not just protecting systems but safeguarding Pakistan’s future.”
He further called for collaborative efforts between government institutions, academia, and industry to build a sustainable cybersecurity ecosystem in Pakistan.
The event concluded with a strong commitment from all stakeholders to support SafeNet’s mission of creating a safer and digitally empowered Pakistan.

In today’s era of rapid digital transformation, cyber threats have become increasingly sophisticated, posing risks not only to individuals and businesses but also to national security and sovereignty. SafeNet seeks to address these challenges by promoting cybersecurity awareness, training, and best practices across academia, industry, and government sectors.
The objectives of the Cyber Awareness Drive include:
Raising awareness about emerging cyber threats and prevention strategies.
Educating participants on cybersecurity hygiene and digital safety practices.
Encouraging students, startups, and professionals to adopt secure technology frameworks.
Providing a platform for networking among cybersecurity experts, academia, and industry leaders.
Showcasing SafeNet’s initiatives and tools for building a secure digital environment.
The initiative targets university students, faculty, startups, entrepreneurs, industry professionals, and tech enthusiasts, making it a nationwide effort to build Pakistan’s cyber resilience.

title: Youth Diplomacy for Climate Change, Kashmir & Palestine Issue
originalTitle: Youth Diplomacy for Climate Change, Kashmir & Palestine Issue
description: President of the Youth Council Pakistan, Muhammad Shehzad Khan, joined a delegation led by Raja Najabat Hussain, Sitara-e-Pakistan and Founding Chairman of the Jammu Kashmir Self Determination Movement International (JKSDMI), for a high-level meeting with Richard Burgon MP, Member of Parliament for Leeds East.
paragraphs: Leeds, UK – August 2025

President of the Youth Council Pakistan, Muhammad Shehzad Khan, joined a delegation led by Raja Najabat Hussain, Sitara-e-Pakistan and Founding Chairman of the Jammu Kashmir Self Determination Movement International (JKSDMI), for a high-level meeting with Richard Burgon MP, Member of Parliament for Leeds East.

The meeting was organised by former Lord Mayor of Leeds, Cllr Asghar Khan Qureshi, at Mr Burgon’s constituency office. The delegation included key JKSDMI leaders including Patron Sardar Abdur Rahman Khan and Administration Director Harry Boota.
Discussions focused on a range of pressing global and regional issues including:
The Kashmir conflict, with emphasis on the demographic changes in Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu & Kashmir (IIOJK),
The ongoing humanitarian situation in Palestine,
The global climate crisis and its disproportionate impact on vulnerable regions,
The role of the United Nations in upholding international law and human rights,
And the rising importance of youth diplomacy in building bridges across cultures and advocating for peace.

President Muhammad Shehzad Khan stressed the need to empower youth voices in international forums and highlighted the efforts of Youth Council Pakistan in mobilising young leaders for climate action and human rights advocacy.

Mr Burgon reiterated his ongoing support for the right to self-determination for the people of Jammu & Kashmir and pledged to continue working with fellow parliamentarians. He also welcomed the invitation to attend upcoming activities in London and Liverpool.

In recognition of their support and contributions, appreciation shields were presented to Richard Burgon MP and Councillor Asghar Khan. Mr Burgon was thanked for his consistent advocacy on human rights issues, while Cllr Asghar Khan was honoured for over 15 years of dedicated service to the Leeds community and the JKSDMI cause.

title: Young Leaders Award Ceremony 2025
description: Youth Council Pakistan proudly hosted the “Young Leaders Award Ceremony 2025” recognizing the exceptional contributions of brilliant young minds who have demonstrated outstanding leadership, dedication, and vision in serving the youth of Pakistan.
paragraphs: Islamabad – September 2025:

Youth Council Pakistan proudly hosted the “Young Leaders Award Ceremony 2025” recognizing the exceptional contributions of brilliant young minds who have demonstrated outstanding leadership, dedication, and vision in serving the youth of Pakistan.

The ceremony was graced by the presence of distinguished guests, including Honourable Ikhtiar Wali Khan, Coordinator to the Prime Minister of Pakistan on Information & Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Affairs as the Chief Guest, along with Mr. Faiz Ullah Faraq (Spokesperson, Government of Gilgit Baltistan), Mr. Adil Khan (Senior Leader PML-N), and Ms. Imtiaz Nasim (MLA/Minister – Government of Azad Jammu & Kashmir).
Speaking at the occasion, Honourable Ikhtiar Wali Khan (Chief Guest) – Coordinator to the Prime Minister of Pakistan on Information & KP Affairs, remarked
“The future of Pakistan rests in the hands of its youth. Platforms like Youth Council Pakistan are shaping that future by grooming ambassadors of change, progress, and unity.”
Faiz Ullah Faraq (Spokesperson – Government of Gilgit Baltistan) said:
“From the mountains of Gilgit Baltistan to the plains of Sindh, the youth are the heartbeat of Pakistan. Today’s recognition proves that young leaders are ready to take charge of tomorrow.”
Adil Khan (Senior Leader PML-N) shared
“Leadership is not about age; it is about vision and service. These awardees have shown that Pakistan’s youth can lead with wisdom, courage, and dedication.”
Ms. Imtiaz Nasim (MLA/Minister – Government of Azad Jammu & Kashmir) stated:
“Youth Council Pakistan is nurturing a generation that will not only lead Pakistan but also represent its true soft image across the world. Our young leaders are the pride of the nation.”

President Muhammad Shehzad Khan emphasized that Youth Council Pakistan serves as an umbrella platform, bringing together young minds from diverse walks of life and providing them with opportunities to be nurtured, groomed, and polished into leaders who represent Pakistan and serve as its ambassadors across the globe.
Young Leaders Award 2025
Awarded to the individuals who served Youth Council Pakistan with utmost passion and dedication over the past years.

The event concluded with a strong reaffirmation of Youth Council Pakistan’s mission to empower and engage the youth, preparing them to take up leadership roles and actively contribute to the nation’s progress.
